 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Squad depth could prove to be secret weapon
 By Lee Sidebotham 
 After another successful week in the Championship for Wanderers, it's easy to forget how many of our current cavalry we haven't even used yet that are still at our disposal.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Josh Sheehan, Sam Dalby and Gaizka Larrazabal are all making the headlines at the moment for their impeccable performances last week. But what about the likes of David Watson, Ryan Hardie and John McAtee?
 Well, I believe they all will still have a part to play as the season goes on. Lest we forget, the Championship is a long old season and we're still only in October. Apart from at right-back, our injury list has been relatively clean so far. But injuries are inevitable in football, especially at this level, and that's when you need to rely on your squad. It's not like previous years in League One, when you could stick someone from the academy on with 15 minutes to go.
 I know what some readers are thinking. The likes of Hardie haven't exactly been up to speed so far this campaign. But that doesn't mean they won't have a part to play this season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Remember when Chris Forino got injured in his first few months and suddenly he was a huge flop? Fans also wrote off Sam Dalby soon after he was fit enough to start in League One last season.
 I mention McAtee, Watson and Hardie because all three scored against Wigan Under-21s in a friendly during the week. Sure, Wigan Under-21s isn't exactly Wolves or Southampton away. To be fair, I still think it's a tougher game than Wigan's senior team at the moment! But that game proved they are ready should they need to come in at some point.
 If you haven't checked out Gary Madine's interview with chief football writer Marc Iles yet, I would highly recommend it. Who would have thought a player like Karl Henry would make such a difference both in the dressing room and on the pitch for the rest of the team? It's easy to forget how much influence one or two people can have within a club, whether they're playing every game or not.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Amario Cozier-Duberry won us, in my opinion at least, 15 points last year alone. While I am not saying the likes of Watson are the next Cozier-Duberry, never underestimate how much one player can do.
 We're in superb form at the moment and in a great position heading into what is the busiest and almost always the deciding part of the football calendar. While right now it feels odd to be thinking about who's not even making the bench, you never quite know when they're going to be needed or called upon.
 Longest Day
 By Chris Evans 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lewis Brunt battles for possession (Image: CameraSport - David Horton) 
 It was an early start for the second longest away trip of the season last Saturday. The sun was shining and the 2,000 Bolton fans were treated to a very entertaining 0-0.
 The game was interesting, with both sides missing very good chances and both having a very good penalty shout declined. It was further evidence that Bolton are able to match the very best this season.
 Lewis Brunt continues to impress at the back. I am looking forward to seeing a Brunt/Forino partnership, but the fact that the latter still hasn't penned a new deal is a bit of a concern after the rumours of discontent last week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Sam Dalby had a thankless task again. He seems to struggle when there is a big physical central defender in opposition. We looked far better when the lively Bair came on. I wonder when he will be given a run of games that he looks to have deserved.
 The highlight for me was seeing Luca Stephenson back in the side after injury. He looked like he had never been away, and more importantly it allowed Larrazabal to venture further forward. We didn't see too much of the attacking flow against a very good opposition, but this combination might go some way to resolving the winger issue against lesser teams, especially given Nelson's injury.
 I'm looking forward to welcoming back Cozier-Duberry on Friday. Boro are one of the strongest sides I've seen this season. But after the way we have played against West Ham, Wolves and Southampton, I'm confident we can give them a game.
 We can compete against anyone
 By Aaron Berriman 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement After midweek success against former Premier League opposition, a trip to fellow former topflight opposition in Southampton gave us chance to back up the victory at Molineux and prove that we can fight against whoever we come up against.
 Let's get the elephant out of the room immediately, the penalty decision. I don't think there can be any complaints regarding the fact that we dodged a bullet on the South Coast, with Ruben Rodrigues the centre of attention for the dubious spot kick decision. Nicknamed, 'the hand of Rod', even from where myself and others were stood at the opposite end of St Mary's, how the penalty wasn't given is beyond me, but it is another valuable point on the board.
 On a positive note, the defensive frailties of old seem to be slowly being extinguished, as another solid performance from the backline returned our third clean sheet of the campaign. Taking a point from Hampshire with a clean sheet to match is some going from the lads, given the fact that the hosts had won every home game since April and had scored in every home game since New Year's Day.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement At the top end of the pitch, we are continuing to create enough chances to get results out of the tougher games. Gaizka Larrazabal had probably the best chance of the afternoon, finding himself in the 18-yard box unmarked, while Rodrigues, Sam Dalby, Josh Sheehan and Kyliane Dong all had moments where they could have snatched the points. As much as the defence is being tested, the frontline are doing what they can to try and turn games back in our favour.
 The Sky cameras are back in town for some Friday night football, as high-flying Middlesbrough come to town, with a certain Amario Cozier-Duberry amongst their ranks. With 5,000 coming down from the North-East, and over 20,000 home fans already securing their seats, it's set to be a blockbuster of a night.
 Remembering how we got here, and January thoughts
 By Daniel Conway 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Theo Bair goes for goal (Image: CameraSport - David Horton) 
 While we near the end of a tough October, we perhaps have the toughest test ahead for us today. High-flying Middlesbrough, with the league's top scorer in Will Lankshear and the return of Super Amario. 
 Like pretty much every game this season, we will have to be at our very best today, and start quickly. It is also important to remember how much we have a role to play today and throughout this season, and remember how far we've not only come this season, but our path to promotion last term as well. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement We thoroughly deserve to be here; all of our late goals last season, smashing Wigan home and away along the way, our memorable play-off semi finals and our day in the scorching capital to top off the campaign. Credit undoubtedly goes to the players for their togetherness and never-say-die attitude, but with Steven Schumacher and his coaching staff, we really do have someone special at the helm at Bolton Wanderers.
 He has taken an expectant fan base in 18 months into the Championship, seen a huge turnover of players, and has really attacked the second tier. What I really like about him is he's not afraid to make mistakes, and will own up to us learning on the job at times. He always wants us to attack, and sets us up to do that no matter the opponents. Long may that continue for an exciting season not only for Bolton Wanderers, but us fans too.
 A few places I think we will look to strengthen in January aren't huge. I am very happy how our backline is looking, through to our midfield. The area for improvement is undoubtedly our wingers. While Gale has vastly improved from last season, the last few games have probably caught up with him from the international break, and it is unfair to put all that emphasis on him. Dong has been a real breath of fresh air, but the verdict is still out on Iling-Junior and Nelson, for me, along with Nelson being out injured now for at least six weeks.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 'Basque Gaz' seems to really shine lately, whatever position he plays in. I think that verdict is still well out on Ryan Hardie at present. I think in January we need to look for another striker profile similar to Johnny Kenny or Dion Charles, even on loan. One who is relentless and likes to run at defenders ankles, never giving them a minute. We saw how well Kenny and Dalby played off each other at times last year. 
 All in all, small details that I'm sure we're already looking into and planning. As for the here and now, it's a visit from promotion-hopefuls Middlesbrough, and the return of last year's star man, super Amario.
 Don't go easy on them, Whites! As always, give it your all and leave it all out there on that pitch. COYWM.
